title: Facebook Pages uses a typed f instead of its logo
observed: The exact grant component renders f. Shared meta_pages mapping separately resolves to meta.com, mixing product and corporate identity.
recommendation: Use an existing local Facebook product asset through one shared icon mapping. Keep Meta corporate identity where appropriate.
acceptance: Pages, Ads and Meta labels each show the intended asset at 16–48px, including fallback.

title: Primary button text fails contrast
observed: Grant Access computes white text on rgb(255,107,53), 18px/600: contrast 2.835:1. Shared primary/brutalist variants repeat this combination. This also exposes a contradiction in the documented button contract.
recommendation: Correct the shared foreground/fill pair and document the accessible pairing. Ink text on coral is a candidate; verify before choosing.
acceptance: All enabled shared variants pass 4.5:1 for ordinary text, or 3:1 where text meets the large-text definition, including hover.

title: Button asChild discards the styled interactive element
observed: Button passes a Fragment containing a span into Radix Slot. Callback links render as adjacent unstyled anchors, each only 24px high. Source consumers include marketing, comparison and callback controls.
recommendation: Pass the actual interactive child to Slot. Preserve icon/loading content inside that child using the existing dependency.
acceptance: Each asChild consumer has one styled, focusable anchor. Its full visible area activates navigation and retains a 44px target.

title: Mobile navigation covers each page on first load
observed: The authenticated layout initializes open=true for desktop and mobile. At 320/390px a full-screen navigation dialog obscures the destination until dismissed.
recommendation: Keep desktop expansion independent from mobile menu visibility. Start the mobile menu closed.
acceptance: Direct visits and navigation show page content first; the menu opens only from its trigger.

title: Mobile menu lacks complete keyboard behavior
observed: The panel declares a modal dialog without focus containment, return focus or Escape handling. Local Escape testing leaves the dialog open at both mobile widths.
recommendation: Use native dialog behavior or a verified accessible primitive for keyboard handling. Restore focus to the menu trigger.
acceptance: Escape closes the panel, Tab stays inside it, background controls cannot receive focus, and focus returns to the opener.

title: Primary content landmarks are inconsistent
observed: Core authenticated previews expose no main landmark. Live home/pricing/about/contact expose two nested main elements; live home also exposes two h1 headings.
recommendation: Give each page one main region and one clear primary heading. Correct ownership at shared layout boundaries.
acceptance: Landmark navigation exposes one named main region on every route; headings reflect the document hierarchy.

title: Recurring navigation has no skip-to-content route
observed: Marketing and authenticated shells have no first-focus skip link. Keyboard users traverse recurring navigation before reaching each destination.
recommendation: Add a visible-on-focus skip link to the unique main region.
acceptance: The first Tab exposes Skip to content; activation moves keyboard focus to the content.

title: Small icon targets remain outside shared sizing
observed: Selected Facebook page removal targets measure 16×16px. Token refresh controls and desktop sidebar collapse use undersized hit areas. Internal filters use 40px heights.
recommendation: Apply the documented 44px hit area through shared icon/button patterns. Preserve visual icon size.
acceptance: Pointer targets meet the project 44px contract without overlapping adjacent controls.

title: Explicit corner radii bypass the square-or-circle rule
observed: Provider groups use rounded-[1rem]. Clerk CSS specifies 8px, .5rem and .75rem. Ordinary rounded-lg/xl utilities already resolve to zero and are excluded.
recommendation: Replace explicit rectangular radii with zero; retain circles for avatars and circular icon controls.
acceptance: Computed styles follow the binary radius contract in provider dialogs and real Clerk widgets.

title: Static cards retain excessive or misleading elevation
observed: Client statistics, headers, request edit cards, partner tables and manual dialogs retain resting soft/hard shadows. Several non-clickable cards gain hover elevation. Live Connections also shows more than three resting filled Connect action shadows in one view.
recommendation: Use existing border-led surfaces. Reserve the three-shadow budget for intentional emphasis and interactive affordances.
acceptance: Review full views, not individual components: <=3 intended shadows; static cards do not imply click behavior.

title: Danger color appears on neutral operations
observed: Onboarding section headings, partner links, admin navigation and ordinary token refresh actions use danger-ink. Warning meaning becomes inconsistent.
recommendation: Use neutral ink for routine operations. Keep danger ink for destructive actions and actual errors.
acceptance: Normal headings/links/refresh actions do not resemble failures; semantic status colors remain consistent.

title: Strict LazyMotion rejects raw motion components in development
observed: The actual AppProviders uses LazyMotion strict. Onboarding and the Clients error branch render raw motion components, causing a development runtime error in the source preview. The development error is not proof of a production outage.
recommendation: Use the existing m primitives inside LazyMotion. Apply existing app motion durations and reduced-motion behavior.
acceptance: Native development routes and error states render without the strict-mode exception; reduced motion remains functional.

title: Go to Dashboard repeats agency creation/update
observed: Final navigation invokes completeOnboarding, which calls resolveAgency again. That helper can POST or PATCH an agency. Agency resolution can encounter duplicate-name rejection; the API create path returns the exact duplicate-name error in the user screenshot. The failing production branch remains unverified.
recommendation: Use the persisted agencyId from link creation for final completion/navigation. Recover missing state explicitly rather than repeating agency mutation.
acceptance: Existing agency, duplicate name, reload/resume and repeated-click cases reach the dashboard once. Confirm the actual failing production network request.

title: Resume restores the step without required request data
observed: Hydration restores agencyId and currentStep but leaves link, request, client, platform and invite data at in-memory defaults. Lifecycle can resume directly at steps 4–6.
recommendation: Hydrate data required by the resumed step from persisted state, or resume at an existing stable request/dashboard destination.
acceptance: Refreshing each post-link step retains the exact request/link/client and truthful invitation state.

title: Final screen shows competing completion controls
observed: The final screen offers Go to Dashboard while the shared footer renders a disabled Complete button. The screenshot confirms the contradiction.
recommendation: Use one completion action. Remove the duplicate final footer control.
acceptance: The final screen presents one enabled, clear completion path on pointer and keyboard.

title: 100% Complete appears before persistence succeeds
observed: Percentage depends on step index, reaching 100% at the final screen before completion API calls succeed.
recommendation: Show Step 7 of 7 until completion is confirmed, or calculate completion from persisted lifecycle.
acceptance: Failed finalization never displays a completed state.

title: Final completion lacks busy state and duplicate-click guard
observed: The raw final button has no disabled/loading state, and the completion handler does not set loading before resolve/persist.
recommendation: Guard the shared completion handler and reflect its pending state in the one final button.
acceptance: Two rapid activations produce one completion operation and an announced pending state.

title: Pending copy assumes Google for every request
observed: Platform selection permits Meta-only and other selections, but generated-link/final/request-success copy says the client must finish Google.
recommendation: Derive copy from requested platforms and actual completion status. Use neutral wording for multi-platform requests.
acceptance: Meta-only, Google-only and multi-platform requests all show accurate next-step instructions.

title: Clipboard promise does not match the action
observed: Platform selection promises automatic clipboard copying. The following screen copies only after explicit activation.
recommendation: Change the promise to match the existing Copy link action; show its actual success/failure.
acceptance: Visible instructions and clipboard behavior match when permissions allow and when copying fails.

title: Team invitations allow duplicate addresses
observed: The context appends without normalization/deduplication. UI keys rows by email. Role buttons also lack selected-state semantics.
recommendation: Normalize and reject duplicate addresses. Use native radios or explicit selected-state semantics for roles.
acceptance: Repeated case-variant email produces one invitation; keyboard/screen reader announces the selected role.

title: Agency validation waits until later steps
observed: The profile permits any nonempty name despite a two-character hint. Server collision errors arrive at create/update, including final navigation.
recommendation: Apply the agreed local name rule at the profile field. Attach server collision feedback to that field at the initial agency operation.
acceptance: Short/duplicate names produce a clear field error with preserved data, before link generation.

title: Team completion wording and counts are unverified
observed: The displayed sent count uses invite-list length. Team-screen copy promises dashboard navigation, but Continue advances to another final screen.
recommendation: Use confirmed invitation results for sent counts and describe the actual next destination.
acceptance: Skip, successful invite, partial failure and resume each display accurate counts and destination copy.

title: Missing request and service failure share one dead end
observed: Request detail labels every fetch failure Request Not Found, without retry/back actions. Success route has a different recovery pattern.
recommendation: Distinguish missing/expired data from transient failures. Reuse one recovery pattern with retry or a clear destination.
acceptance: 404 and 503 produce different guidance; a recovered service can reload the same request.

title: Missing-platform submission error disappears
observed: The context moves PLATFORMS_NOT_CONNECTED failures back to step 2; the page only displays state.error in step 4.
recommendation: Render the error at the shared wizard level or at the destination step, with the required connection action.
acceptance: Simulated missing-platform response shows an explanation on Platforms, preserves the draft and allows recovery.

title: Edit Back bypasses the discard confirmation
observed: The prominent Back control calls router.back. Only beforeunload is guarded; footer discard already uses a confirmation.
recommendation: Route the Back control through the existing discard dialog.
acceptance: Dirty form + Back offers Keep editing/Discard; keeping retains every value. Clean forms navigate directly.

title: Cancel request failure has no user feedback
observed: The cancellation handler has try/finally without catch. A rejected mutation cannot show a useful recovery message in the dialog.
recommendation: Display the error in the existing confirmation and allow retry. Preserve the active request when cancellation fails.
acceptance: A simulated 503 keeps request state accurate and presents a clear retry path.

title: Request actions nest buttons inside links
observed: Action-bar Link elements wrap Button components, creating nested interactive controls.
recommendation: Use a single styled link after fixing S03, or the established link styling.
acceptance: Each action exposes exactly one keyboard focus target and one accessible role.

title: Request review exposes raw platform group identifiers
observed: The new-request summary renders raw group keys such as google instead of shared display names. Live Review confirms google (6).
recommendation: Use PLATFORM_NAMES consistently in review and related approval views.
acceptance: Google, Meta and LinkedIn group labels use consistent display names; product selections remain understandable.

title: Success page permanently labels a request pending
observed: The success route uses fixed pending copy despite loading current request data. Revisiting a completed request can contradict its detail view.
recommendation: Render the current persisted status and matching next action.
acceptance: Revisit pending, partial, completed, revoked and expired requests; success/detail views agree.

title: Manual flows retry expired or revoked invitations
observed: Main invite uses a terminal card for dead links. Manual flow maps every load error to a retry card.
recommendation: Reuse the existing terminal classifier/card in all six manual flows.
acceptance: Expired/revoked links show agency-contact guidance; transient failures offer retry.

title: Manual validation is disconnected from its field
observed: Manual form errors are visually present without aria-invalid or aria-describedby.
recommendation: Associate errors with their inputs and announce submission outcomes using existing form patterns.
acceptance: Invalid manual input has an announced error and a stable association; valid submission clears it.

title: Filters changes tint but does not filter
observed: Click only toggles showFilters. No filter panel or query change consumes that state.
recommendation: Remove the unsupported control, or wire the filters required by the current product using existing query inputs.
acceptance: Every visible filter changes results and provides a clear reset state.

title: Clients after the first page cannot be reached
observed: The query omits pagination, backend defaults to a finite page, and UI reports total without pagination/load-more controls. The synthetic fixture displays one of 61.
recommendation: Use the existing paginated API contract to expose subsequent records.
acceptance: An account with more clients than one API page can reach/search the last record and correctly reports current results versus total.

title: Client identifiers truncate without inspection
observed: List name/company/email use truncate without title/details reveal. Search has only a placeholder label; no-result copy offers no reset.
recommendation: Allow full identifier inspection, name the search input and provide Clear search in the filtered empty state.
acceptance: Long names/emails remain distinguishable at 320px; search has a name; reset restores results.

title: Client detail exceeds its mobile container
observed: Actual route preview with a long client name/email has a 402px scroll area inside a 318px container at 320px. Header badge/email and fixed padding force horizontal scrolling. The existing mixed-Google harness also shows collisions.
recommendation: Reduce narrow padding, wrap the heading/status/actions and break long identifiers. Keep dates aligned without overlap.
acceptance: At 320px/390px and 200% zoom, long client data produces no unintended horizontal scrolling or overlapping labels.

title: Client tabs use a different keyboard model
observed: Client tabs declare role=tab but keep all tabs in sequence and omit Arrow/Home/End handlers. Settings already implements the correct reusable behavior.
recommendation: Reuse the existing settings tab keyboard behavior.
acceptance: Arrow/Home/End moves selected focus correctly; one tab is in the tab sequence and its panel is associated.

title: Filtered empty state asks to create another request
observed: Overview reuses a create-request message when existing requests simply do not match a status filter.
recommendation: Show filter-specific copy and a Clear filter action. Keep creation guidance for genuinely empty clients.
acceptance: Every status filter distinguishes no matching results from no requests.

title: Client overlays lack the common dialog contract
observed: Create Client, Delete Client and Create Request use generic motion containers without complete dialog/focus behavior. Create labels lack htmlFor/IDs and the close icon has no name. Live Create Client exposes zero dialog roles, four fields without associated labels, and one unnamed close button. Edit Client has dialog/Escape semantics but still lacks focus containment.
recommendation: Use one accessible dialog shell with native dialog behavior or a verified installed primitive. Associate labels and name the close action.
acceptance: All overlays have a name, initial/return focus, Tab containment and Escape; fields expose labels and failures.

title: Token Health columns overlap and clip on mobile
observed: The fixed twelve-column grid compresses five desktop columns into 320px. The local bottom-of-page capture shows client text, Healthy badge, expiry and action header colliding; overflow-hidden masks the defect. The 320px production view independently confirms overlap between real client email, Healthy badge and expiry.
recommendation: Use labeled stacked rows at narrow widths, or an intentional accessible scroll table.
acceptance: Long identifiers/status/expiry/actions remain readable at 320px and 200% zoom; every row action remains reachable.

title: Refresh token health has no accessible name
observed: The page-header refresh button contains only an icon and has no aria-label. Browser DOM inspection confirms an unnamed control.
recommendation: Name the control and announce loading/result state. Apply S08 sizing.
acceptance: Accessibility tree exposes Refresh token health and loading does not erase its name.

title: Checkout reports activation without server confirmation
observed: Checkout success says the subscription is active without fetching current subscription. Billing toast says upgraded whenever checkout=success is present.
recommendation: Reuse the billing query and show a verification/pending state until persisted subscription status confirms activation.
acceptance: Delayed webhook, failed checkout, stale/bookmarked and edited query URLs never falsely assert upgrade.

title: Billing details save has no result feedback
observed: The handler awaits mutateAsync without local error handling or visible success. The mutation only invalidates data. Existing pending/disabled behavior is present and is not counted as missing.
recommendation: Use existing inline feedback/toast patterns for success and failure; preserve edited values on failure.
acceptance: A failed save shows an actionable error; a successful save confirms persistence without losing focus.

title: Several load failures have no recovery action
observed: Clients, connections, webhooks, token health and unavailable agent approvals render errors without a consistent retry or destination. Partner approval misclassification is tracked separately.
recommendation: Apply the existing recovery card pattern with error-specific copy and retry/back actions.
acceptance: 503→200 recovery works in place on each surface. True missing/unavailable records offer a clear next destination.

title: Dialog code loading uses a page-card fallback
observed: Connections dynamic imports render a page-width min-height placeholder before the real provider overlay. Slow code loading changes the visual shell.
recommendation: Keep the existing dialog shell while loading its body, or show pending state on the initiating control.
acceptance: Throttled code loading does not move the page or present an unrelated card before the overlay.

title: Diagnostic and checkout pages use legacy visual tokens
observed: Token Health uses slate/indigo. Checkout results use green/amber gradients, large blurred shadows and a 500ms entrance. Client detail boundaries also use legacy slate/shadows. Redirecting settings/platforms uses indigo.
recommendation: Use existing paper/ink/semantic status tokens, shared loading shells and app motion tokens.
acceptance: Loading→loaded→error transitions preserve visual hierarchy and work with reduced motion and dark theme.

title: Agent approvals expose machine names
observed: Approval platform and permission chips print raw values. Current status already replaces underscores, so status itself is not counted as an underscore defect.
recommendation: Use shared product names and readable permission labels without weakening the precise effect preview.
acceptance: Pending/terminal approvals show clear platform, permission, target and effect labels, including long values.

title: Settings labels mix capitalization conventions
observed: General, billing and webhooks mix Title Case with sentence-case sections and controls.
recommendation: Apply one existing sentence-case convention consistently to labels/actions.
acceptance: All four tabs use consistent section, field and action casing.

title: Dashboard repeats filled Create request actions
observed: Header and recent-request section both expose filled create actions. Checklist variants add further prominence.
recommendation: Keep one primary visible create action and make the repeated contextual action secondary.
acceptance: Populated/checklist/empty views each retain an obvious creation path without competing emphasis.

title: Footer section links stay on the wrong page
observed: Live pricing footer Features leaves the URL and scroll position unchanged after activation. Handler prevents default and only searches the current DOM. Live home does contain both section IDs; the nav already supports cross-route hashes.
recommendation: Route footer links to the homepage sections, reusing the nav behavior.
acceptance: Features and How it works reach the named home sections from pricing, blog and contact using pointer and keyboard.

title: Blog subscription form has no subscription action
observed: The newsletter form has no action/onSubmit, input name or integration. It promises weekly tips but cannot create a subscription.
recommendation: Connect to an existing supported list endpoint, or remove the unsupported form/promise. Give the email field a persistent label.
acceptance: Submission creates a real subscription and reports success/failure, or the nonfunctional form is absent.

title: Article Schedule Demo points to #
observed: The article CTA is an anchor with href=# and no scheduling handler.
recommendation: Use the existing scheduling modal or contact destination.
acceptance: Mouse and keyboard activation opens a real scheduling path.

title: Comparison template uses a second visual system
observed: The general comparison template uses teal accents/text, custom colors and blurred resting shadows. This affects all slugs routed through that template; other comparison templates need separate checks.
recommendation: Update the shared template to existing tokens and border-led surfaces once.
acceptance: Representative pages from each template match the documented palette and pass measured contrast.

title: Desktop marquee moves under reduced motion
observed: Live home with reducedMotion=reduce still changes both inline and computed transforms across 1.2 seconds. CSS and Framer Motion both animate the track.
recommendation: Use the existing static grid when reduced motion is requested, and suppress both animation paths.
acceptance: Reduced-motion desktop/mobile show static readable content with no transform changes over time.

title: Public guide routes unexpectedly require authentication
observed: Both published guides navigate signed-out visitors to accounts.authhub.co instead of rendering content. The proxy public allowlist omits /guides and protects everything else.
recommendation: Include the published guide route family in the public routing contract, with a focused regression check.
acceptance: Signed-out visits to both canonical guides return their content without the login/security challenge.

title: Article raises a hydration mismatch in production
observed: The Google Ads article consistently emits React error #418 at 1440, 390 and 320px. Cause is unconfirmed. Locale-dependent date formatting is one candidate, not a proven diagnosis.
recommendation: Locate the exact mismatched markup/text and make server/client output deterministic.
acceptance: The article renders without hydration errors across locale/timezone and narrow/wide viewports.

title: Pricing reveal causes temporary horizontal overflow under reduced motion
observed: Before viewport reveals settle, live pricing measures 324px at 320px and 394px at 390px. The offscreen savings panel starts at x:+20. After scrolling through the page, width returns to 320/390px. This is a reveal-state defect, not settled grid overflow.
recommendation: Suppress reveal transforms under reduced motion; ensure hidden/offscreen panels cannot widen the document.
acceptance: At 320/390px with reduced motion, initial and scrolled states stay inside the viewport without horizontal movement.

title: Partner load failures claim approval is pending
observed: Any error or absent data produces Access pending approval, including service/network failures.
recommendation: Distinguish approval state from load failure and provide retry for the latter.
acceptance: A network 503 never changes the displayed account approval status.

title: Campaign errors lack field and announcement associations
observed: The campaign error renders after submit without field association or live announcement. Referral URL also truncates without full visual inspection, although Copy already works.
recommendation: Associate campaign feedback with its field. Provide full referral URL inspection on keyboard/pointer without removing Copy.
acceptance: Invalid campaign feedback is announced; full referral URL is inspectable at narrow widths.

title: Admin search inputs rely on placeholders
observed: Agencies and webhooks search controls lack associated visible/accessible labels and use 40px height.
recommendation: Use named search fields and the documented target sizing. Keep existing server filters.
acceptance: Admin searches expose names and retain usable focus/targets at narrow widths and zoom.

title: Provider dialogs allow focus behind the overlay
observed: ManageAssetsModalShell supplies dialog semantics and Escape but no initial/return focus or Tab containment. In live Google settings, Shift+Tab from Done twice focuses the background Connect button.
recommendation: Use native dialog behavior or a verified installed accessible primitive for the shared shell. Keep the existing provider bodies.
acceptance: Tab/Shift+Tab remain in the modal; background controls cannot activate; dismissal restores the Manage assets opener.

title: Meta asset toggles have no accessible names
observed: Five top-level Meta asset checkboxes expose no label in the live dialog. Source renders inputs beside paragraph labels without association. Google already names its equivalent toggles.
recommendation: Associate each checkbox with its asset name/description and use the existing named checkbox pattern.
acceptance: Screen readers announce Enable Ad Account, Page, Catalog, Dataset and Instagram Account, plus checked state.

title: An established workspace intermittently opens first-time setup
observed: From a live dashboard with 12 requests and 12 active connections, the first Clients navigation redirected to onboarding Step 1. Later Clients/Settings visits loaded the existing agency. The triggering lookup/cache/guard branch is unconfirmed.
recommendation: Trace the cold-navigation agency/status lookup and redirect cache. Keep transient lookup failure distinct from a confirmed absent/incomplete agency.
acceptance: Cold and warm navigation to every protected route consistently preserves the existing workspace; genuine new agencies still enter onboarding.

title: Valid request statuses fall back to Unknown
observed: Live dashboard request rows and request detail show Unknown. Their callers cast request status as any; shared StatusBadge has no completed or partial configurations. These are valid request lifecycle values.
recommendation: Add explicit supported request lifecycle presentations or a typed request-status adapter. Remove the casts that bypass the contract.
acceptance: Pending, partial, completed, expired and revoked each render a clear, accurate label on dashboard/detail/success.

title: Request, connection and platform statuses lack clear domain labels
observed: For one live request, the platform board says Revoked, its history row says Active, and detail says Unknown plus Waiting on client authorization. Some statuses describe different domains; the UI does not explain that distinction.
recommendation: Label request lifecycle and connection/asset health separately. Use typed shared mappings without forcing distinct domain states into one generic badge.
acceptance: A request with an active connection but unfinished/revoked asset requirements shows both facts accurately, with clear next action and agreement across views.

title: Total Requests on the client list counts connections
observed: Live list reports Total Requests:1, while the same client detail reports 12. Source binds the Total Requests label to client.connectionCount.
recommendation: Render the actual request count, or relabel the existing metric accurately if the list contract intentionally exposes only connection count.
acceptance: List/detail use the same request-count definition; connection count has its own label.

title: Mobile billing withholds plan details and tier actions
observed: Below md, comparison shows only tier name/persona/price and Full plan details available on larger screens. Features and tier actions exist only in the desktop grid. Live 758px billing confirms this restriction.
recommendation: Provide an existing stacked/expandable comparison at narrow widths, or a clear link to complete accessible plan details.
acceptance: Mobile users can compare included capabilities and select the intended tier without changing devices.

title: Connected Google empty states give no useful recovery
observed: Live connected Google settings show No accounts available for Business Profile/Merchant Center, followed by Connect your account first. Those product sections have no direct recovery action or explanation of missing access versus missing assets.
recommendation: Use product-specific empty-state guidance and expose an appropriate existing reload/account-management path. Do not imply the whole Google connection is absent.
acceptance: Connected-but-empty, permission failure and disconnected cases show distinct guidance and an actionable next step.

title: Request customization has an unnamed removal action
observed: Live Customize exposes an icon-only field removal button with no accessible name. Source confirms the Trash2 button has no aria-label or text. Repeated Review Edit buttons also lack section-specific names.
recommendation: Name removal with its field label and each edit action with its section. Use the existing shared icon-button sizing contract.
acceptance: Screen readers distinguish Remove Company Website, Edit client, Edit platforms, Edit access level and Edit form fields; removal has a 44px target.
